calls.head: Calgary shoots far more than Vancouver
calls.body: On shot volume, Calgary sits 12th of 32, at the relentless end of the scale. Vancouver is 30th, at the selective end.
calls.call: Calgary takes more 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than Vancouver.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, Calgary had 80.7 per 60 and Vancouver 58.0 per 60. Coming in, Calgary was at 58.8 per 60 and Vancouver at 48.6 per 60.

calls.head: Point-blank against perimeter
calls.body: Vancouver ranks 15th of 32 for shot quality, toward the point-blank end; Calgary ranks 31st, toward the perimeter end.
calls.call: Vancouver’s shots are more dangerous on average than Calgary’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average unblocked shot was, Vancouver had 1 goal per 14.8 shots and Calgary 1 goal per 24.3 shots. Coming in, Vancouver was at 1 goal per 15.8 shots and Calgary at 1 goal per 17.0 shots.
calls.usual: VAN 1 goal per 15.8 shots · CGY 1 goal per 17.0 shots
calls.tonight: VAN 1 goal per 14.8 shots · CGY 1 goal per 24.3 shots

VAN.head: We had this close to even (52% for Vancouver), and Vancouver came through.

CGY.head: We had this close to even (48% for Calgary), and it went Vancouver’s way.

surprises.head: Vancouver brought the hits
surprises.body: Vancouver’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 160, against its usual 82 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Vancouver tried a different line
surprises.body: E. Pettersson, L. Karlsson, M. Rossi played 10:30 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Vancouver’s usual lines.
